title: People’s Mañanera October 2
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**October 2: Remembrance, Truth, and Never Again Repression  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum recalled the repression of the 1968 student
movement in Tlatelolco and noted that the state had acknowledged then
president Díaz Ordaz’s responsibility. She reiterated: “Never again will the
state repress a social movement.”

**Protecting Youth and Addressing the Root Causes of Violence  
** Following the attack at a middle school in Coahuila, the President
announced a decree requiring online platforms to detect, report, and remove
content that incites violence, abuse, or harassment. The “ABC of Emotions” and
the “Line of Life” programs will be strengthened. Sheinbaum added that “we
will do whatever it takes to protect children and young people.”

**Culture and Arts Education for Transformation  
** Cultural events attracted 50 million participants; 1.85 billion pesos
(US$83.34 million) were earmarked for educational spaces, and funding for
creative projects increased by 45%. IMCINE grew by 25%; EFICA, an incentive
program for producing in Mexico, will receive 400 million pesos (US$22.23
million); and the Carlos Chávez School Orchestra now has its own
installations.

**National heritage artefacts and culture returned to the people  
** Mexico recovered 5,686 archaeological artifacts—17,000 since 2018—and
invested 520 million pesos (US$28.89 million) in archaeological sites and
museums. In addition, 2,600 workers in the sector were reclassified with a 17%
pay increase; a zero sales tax rate is proposed for bookstores; and 3.5
million books will be distributed.
